title: Runway Briefing — Alaska Bets Big on Beds, Boeing's MAX 10 Gets Benched Again, and a Tiny Island Runway Nobody's Heard Of
summary: Alaska Airlines just dropped its biggest product overhaul ever — lie-flat seats on 737s, new suites, new lounges, the works — as it tries to catch up to the big three. Meanwhile Boeing's 737 MAX 10 hits another delay after United and Southwest straight-up refuse to take jets with a software bug Boeing sat on for two years. Plus, why a runway on a tiny Pacific atoll matters way more than it should, and Canada's airports might be about to get a $36 billion new landlord.
